newsitem.title: JAPAN: No talks on LNG stakes with Qatar - Japan traders.
newsitem.headline: No talks on LNG stakes with Qatar - Japan traders.

text.p: Officials from Japanese trading houses will not be meeting Qatar's visiting energy minister to discuss the possible purchase of stakes in Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG Co (Rasgas), traders said on Wednesday.

Energy and Industry Minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah is in Japan for a ceremony marking the first liquefied natural gas (LNG) vessel to carry Qatari term gas cargoes to Japan. He will be here until October 5.
Japan's Chubu Electric Power Co Inc will import four million tonnes of LNG a year from Qatar Liquefied Gas Company (Qatargas) for 25 years starting 1997.

As the minister's activities in Japan are mainly related to the Qatargas project, no talks will take place between the Qatari side and the Japanese trading houses on the possible purchase of the Rasgas stakes, traders said.
Sumitomo Corp, Nissho Iwai Corp and Itochu Corp have been seeking to acquire a combined 10 percent stake in Rasgas, traders said.
Rasgas, which is expected to produce 10 million tonnes of LNG a year starting 1999, is currently 70 percent owned by Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC), and the remainder by Mobil Corp.
